title: Why You Should Include SAP Value Chain Analysis (VCA) in Your RISE - Bill of Materials
author: christinediaz
text:
Many customers are looking to understand, what makes SAP's core S/4HANA Private, Cloud ERP stand out amongst our competitors. SAP’s VCA solution is an example of better bang for your buck as it part of the core S/4HANA ERP, Private cloud addition. Many features are already included in the core license such as Advanced Intercompany Processing. which includes an embedded solution that creates the required intercompany processes automatically in the background. 
 However, the latest release, 2025 (FPS1) adds more functionality with multi-stage intercompany processes; creating automated intercompany documents while bridging together both finance and logistics information all in one framework for a true end-to-end tracking of product level details. All visible in the VCA dashboard for document flow and status visibility for the end users. The benefits the VCA solution bring significant efficiencies across a global enterprise as it enables streamlined best practice processes with automation and implementation cost savings.

title: Create Time Dependent Dimension with Multiple Time Dependent Sources
author: vineet_gupta3
text: SAP Datasphere offers clears guidance on how to model a dimension view where attributes are time dependent. It gets complicated when you have attributes from multiple sources, each with independent time intervals. One approach is to have independent time dependent views for each source and then daisy chain them with associations to achieve the final dimension view. This blog provides an alternate approach using sql view to merge time intervals for each source and still maintain correct values for all attributes.

title: Enterprise Solution Development with SAP Joule Studio
author: hkaur
text: Introduction Joule Studio is SAP's AI-first development environment that enables organisations to build and deploy enterprise-grade agents, workflows, and applications simply by describing what they want to achieve. This blog walks through its key capabilities, how it works, and the value it brings to businesses running on SAP. At its core, Joule Studio provides low-code capabilities to build and operate AI agents, automated workflows, and applications all governed by the enterprise-grade controls and deep business understanding that SAP systems demand. The platform is accessible through two complementary paths: Joule Studio Web UI A conversational, browser-based experience that allows business users and citizen developers to describe what they want in plain language and watch the platform translate that description into a working solution. Joule Studio CLI A command-line interface designed for professional developers who prefer working within their local IDE while following the same intent-based methodology. Both paths share the same underlying philosophy: intent-based development, which anchors every solution firmly in real business objectives rather than technical abstractions. The Intent-Based Development Model The most distinctive characteristic of Joule Studio is its intent-based development model. Rather than asking developers to begin with architecture diagrams, API catalogues, or data models, Joule Studio starts with a simple question: What outcome do you need? This approach is captured in a structured, six-step process. While the steps represent a logical progression, they are deliberately non-linear. Teams can revisit earlier stages after reviewing generated artefacts, refine their intent once they see the automatically produced specification, or loop back to adjust requirements after testing. Step 1: Intent The journey begins when a user describes their business challenge and the solution they envision in natural language. After the intent is defined, Joule Studio initiates a solution discovery process, consulting multiple SAP knowledge sources to design an architecturally sound solution within the constraints of the customer's specific SAP landscape. Users who want to move quickly can use the Quick Create option to bypass clarifying questions and proceed directly to solution generation. Step 2: Requirements Once the intent has been validated and enriched through discovery, all gathered information is synthesized into a formal Product Requirements Document (PRD). This document contains structured user personas, requirements expressed as user stories, explicit scope boundaries, and a high-level architectural overview. Step 3: Specification The next phase is specification phase, generating an implementation blueprint. This blueprint encompasses architecture decisions, API references, data models, and a prioritised task list. Joule Studio automatically discovers relevant SAP APIs from the SAP Business Accelerator Hub, sparing developers from the time-consuming task of searching through hundreds of available APIs manually. Step 4: Solution This is where code becomes reality. Based on the approved specification, Joule Studio generates production-ready agents, automations, and applications precisely tailored to the customer's SAP landscape. These are not generic templates but they are architecture-aware artefacts that reflect the systems, deployment models, and integration patterns already in place. Step 5: Testing Before anything reaches production, the solution is deployed to an isolated sandbox environment for thorough validation. The testing step allows developers and business users to interact with the solution, verify that it meets stated requirements and success criteria defined during PRD phase, and confirm that it behaves correctly against real data and system interactions. Step 6: Deployment The final step sees the solution transition from development to production. It is worth noting that the developer's responsibility at this stage is to validate the solution in development. Solution Discovery Joule Studio consults multiple intelligence sources before proposing any solution architecture. SAP LeanIX : Enterprise Landscape Understanding SAP LeanIX provides context about the customer's specific SAP environment: which systems are deployed and how the organisation is structured. This contextual grounding ensures that proposed solutions actually work within the customer's real landscape. SAP Knowledge Graph : API Discovery and Architecture Mapping The SAP Knowledge Graph maps business needs to SAP's Reference Business Architecture. It identifies relevant APIs with their full specifications and authentication requirements, and it performs a fit-gap analysis that determines which capabilities already exist in standard SAP offerings versus which aspects require custom development. SAP Domain Models : Best Practices and Intelligence SAP Domain Models guide the solution towards proven architecture patterns, appropriate security and compliance controls, and established SAP design patterns. SAP Signavio: Process Insights SAP Signavio supplies process intelligence that give insights into how business processes are actually running which in turn helps to ground the proposed solution in real, observed process behaviour within the organization. Accessing Joule Studio Via Joule Work: The primary access point for most users is through Joule Work , SAP's intelligent workspace UI. Users navigate to Joule Studio by selecting Develop from the main navigation bar within Joule Work. The integration is intentional. Because Joule Work already understands the user's role, context, and connected systems, the transition into development mode is seamless. Via the CLI: For professional developers, the CLI provides a code-first path that integrates with any modern IDE. Developers can follow the same intent-based process — describing their intent in a configuration file, generating specifications and the final solution. Solution Types in Joule Studio Joule Studio supports distinct types of solutions( rapidly evolving), each addressing different automation and intelligence scenarios. Agents: Agents are the centrepiece capability of Joule Studio. An agent understands natural language, accesses SAP data, and executes tasks through conversation. What an Agent Can Do : A Joule Studio agent possesses several core capabilities: Natural language comprehension — Users ask questions or give commands in plain language, without needing to frame requests in technical terms. SAP system connectivity — The agent connects to SAP S/4HANA and other SAP systems through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools . This provides a secure, governed connection to backend data. Tool execution — Agents can invoke specific actions such as querying financial data, analysing operational trends, or generating insights from business records. Contextual decision-making — The agent determines which APIs to call based on the context of a conversation, without the user needing to specify technical details. Agent-to-agent communication — Through the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol, agents can discover and invoke other agents, enabling orchestrated multi-agent workflows that tackle complex, multi-domain tasks. Agent Skills : Within the agent architecture, "skills" represent discrete capabilities. A skill might be retrieving invoice data from SAP, calculating a financial impact across a date range, or summarising supplier performance across a quarter. Skills define the scope of agent action and are exposed to Joule's routing engine. SAP System Connectivity and Security : Agents access SAP backends through a secure, governed gateway — the Agent Gateway which serves as the single controlled connection point between agents and SAP systems. Automatic Discovery Through Joule : Once deployed, an agent becomes automatically discoverable through Joule. When a user asks a question that falls within the agent's declared area of responsibility, Joule routes that request to the agent transparently. SAP Managed n8n Workflows: Structured Process Automation: Joule Studio provides SAP Managed n8n Workflows — a workflow automation tool that orchestrates multi-step business processes within SAP's governed environment. A workflow is composed of nodes — building blocks that retrieve, process, transform, or transmit data. Nodes are connected sequentially, with each node consuming the output of its predecessor. The workflow begins with a trigger that determines when and how the automation starts, followed by one or more processing nodes. What Workflows Enable The range of automation scenarios addressable through SAP Managed n8n is broad: Approval automation: Route documents, invoices, or procurement requests through multi-level approval chains. Deliver approval tasks directly to SAP Task Center for streamlined action. Business Rules and Conditional Branching : Workflows support conditional logic described in natural language. For instance: if an invoice amount is below a specified threshold, approve it automatically; if it exceeds that threshold, route it to a manager for review. Joule Studio translates the plain language description into the corresponding workflow branching logic, eliminating the need for manual configuration. Workflow Node Architecture : Nodes are the operational units of a workflow. In Joule Studio, two categories of nodes are available: Standard n8n Nodes, SAP-Specific Nodes that have Pre built SAP Connectors. Agent Extensions : Dynamic Customisation at Runtime : Beyond standalone agents and automated workflows, Joule Studio introduces a third solution type: Agent Extensions. These provide capailities to customise and extend existing agent capabilities dynamically at runtime, without requiring modification of the base agent itself. Agent Extensions are valuable in scenarios where users can Inject organisation-specific logic or policy constraints into an agent's behaviour without altering its core architecture. Creating a Solution The Web UI Walkthrough : For users working through the Web UI, creating a solution follows a straightforward process: 1. Open Joule Work and navigate to the Develop section from the main navigation bar. 2. Select the solution type — choose from an Agent tile, an n8n Workflow tile, or an Agent Extension tile, or describe the challenge in the chat window and let Joule Studio recommend the appropriate type. 3. Provide the solution details — enter a name for the solution and an intent statement that describes the goal. For agent extensions, use the Agent Catalog to select the target agent. 4. Choose the creation mode — either enable Quick Create to proceed immediately without clarifying questions, or use the guided approach. 5. Select Create — Joule Studio initiates the discovery and generation process. Solution Artefacts, Git Integration, and Collaboration Solution Artefacts: Each solution produced by Joule Studio consists of one or more solution artefacts — discrete components that can be configured, tested, and deployed independently. This granularity supports modular development patterns and enables teams to stage the rollout of complex multi-component solutions. Connecting to Git : Joule Studio integrates with Git repositories, enabling teams to manage their generated code using standard version control practices. This Git connectivity is essential for the deployment handoff process, as the production deployment pipeline is triggered from the GitHub repository to which the developer pushes the validated solution. Solution Collaboration : Enterprise solutions are rarely the work of a single individual. Joule Studio's collaboration feature allows solution owners to share access with colleagues, enabling joint development within the same solution context. As the owner, you control precisely who can access the solution and what level of involvement each collaborator is permitted — aligning with standard ent

title: Relembre a palestra: SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2, a evolução do CRM da SAP #SITCWB2026
author: AdrianoCWB
text:
No dia 7 de novembro, no Auditório Gregor Mendel da PUCPR, Clóvis Müller, Consultor Funcional SAP Sales & Service Cloud, com 12 anos de experiência em CRM, apresentou no SAP Inside Track Curitiba 2026 a palestra "Conheça o SAP Sales & Service Cloud Versão 2: A Evolução do CRM da SAP". 
 Sobre a palestra 
 Clóvis apresentou a Versão 2 do SAP Sales & Service Cloud, dentro da suíte SAP Customer Experience. Todas as soluções conectam-se pelo SAP BTP, com integrações pré-configuradas e fluxo de dados em tempo real. 
 A evolução do SAP CRM 
 Até 2013: SAP CRM, on-premise (o mais usado foi o 7.0). 
 2013 a 2016: SAP Hybris, após a compra da Hybris. 
 2018: SAP C/4HANA. 
 2020: SAP Sales & Service Cloud, conhecido como C4C. 
 2023: SAP Sales & Service Cloud Versão 2, plataforma cloud-native baseada em microsserviços e APIs, com IA. Segundo a palestra, não é só uma atualização, é uma reestruturação completa. 
 O que mostrou na prática 
 Sales Cloud: visão 360° do cliente, ciclo de vendas do lead ao pedido, gestão de oportunidades, da oportunidade à cotação, dashboards e uso pelo celular. 
 Service Cloud: atendimento multicanal (chat, e-mail, telefone, WhatsApp), identificação automática do cliente, base de conhecimento, SLAs e criação de solicitações. 
 Recursos de IA: pontuação de leads, resumo da conta e análise de sentimento. 
 Para aprender mais 
 A palestra indicou o SAP Help Portal e o SAP Learning para documentação e treinamentos. 
 Sobre o palestrante 
 Clóvis Müller, consultor SAP Sales Cloud e Service Cloud, certificado SAP nas versões 1 e 2 das duas soluções. 
 Assista à palestra no YouTube: https://youtu.be/626HpynZd7U 
 Veja todas as palestras no post índice: https://community.sap.com/t5/curitiba-blog-posts/sap-inside-track-curitiba-2026-relembre-as-palestras-sitcwb/ba-p/14522453

title: SAP DM MQTT Broker: Is Certificate Update Required When Leaf Certificate Rotates?
author: ankit12
text:
Hi Experts, 
 We have configured connectivity between SAP Digital Manufacturing (SAP DM) Production Connector and a third-party MQTT broker using the Manage Message Brokers application in our production environment. 
 Currently, we have uploaded a single PEM file containing the complete certificate chain , consisting of: 
 Root CA Certificate: Remains unchanged. 
 Intermediate CA Certificate: Remains unchanged. 
 Leaf (Server) Certificate: Automatically rotates approximately every 30 days. 
 Since the MQTT broker's leaf certificate is periodically renewed, we would like clarification on the following: 

 Certificate Rotation: When the MQTT broker's leaf certificate rotates, do we need to upload the updated PEM file containing the complete certificate chain again in SAP DM's Manage Message Brokers application? 

 CA-Based Trust: If the Root and Intermediate CA certificates remain unchanged, will SAP DM Production Connector automatically trust the renewed leaf certificate without requiring any manual certificate update? 

 Certificate Chain Validation: When a PEM file contains all three certificates, does SAP DM Production Connector validate the renewed leaf certificate against the trusted Root/Intermediate CA, or does it require the exact leaf certificate originally uploaded? 

 Recommended Configuration: Can we configure only the Root and Intermediate CA certificates in the PEM file to avoid updating the certificate configuration whenever the leaf certificate rotates? 

 Connectivity Impact: Does leaf certificate rotation require any configuration redeployment or Production Connector restart to maintain MQTT connectivity? Our objective is to ensure uninterrupted MQTT connectivity without manually updating the certificate configuration every 30 days. Please help us with the right approach to resolve this. Quick response will be appreciated. Regards, Ankit Gupta

title: Issue with time zone token in interview scheduling (Canada - Alberta, British Columbia)

title: Asset Accounting- Depreciation calculation change from Gross to Net
author: nag_7589
text:
Hello Experts, 
 We have two company codes using SAP Asset Accounting: 
 GR01 (Germany) – Asset Accounting implemented in 1996 
 C001 (Canada) – Asset Accounting implemented in 2025 
 We noticed that depreciation postings are handled differently between the two company codes. 
 1. Germany (GR01) – Gross Method 
 Asset acquisition: 
 Dr Technical Equipment (Asset G/L 100000) = 100,000 
 Cr Vendor 
 Monthly depreciation posting: 
 Dr Depreciation Expense (G/L 7000 - Deduction for wear and tear) 
 Cr Asset Reconciliation Account (G/L 100000) 
 As a result, depreciation is posted directly against the asset account. 
 2. Canada (C001) – Net Method 
 Asset acquisition: 
 Dr Technical Equipment (Asset G/L 100000) = 100,000 
 Cr Vendor 
 Monthly depreciation posting: 
 Dr Depreciation Expense (G/L 7000 - Deduction for wear and tear) 
 Cr Accumulated Depreciation (G/L 200000) 
 In this case, the asset acquisition cost remains unchanged and depreciation is accumulated on a separate accumulated depreciation account. 
 Requirement 
 We would like to understand how to change the German company code from the current gross posting method to the net posting method , similar to the Canadian setup. 
 Questions 
 Which SAP Asset Accounting configuration determines whether depreciation is posted using the gross or net method? 
 Is this controlled by: 
 Depreciation Area settings? 
 Account Determination (AO90)? 
 Transaction types? 
 Another configuration object? 
 What is the recommended procedure to switch an existing company code from gross to net depreciation posting? 
 What impact would this change have on: 
 Existing fixed assets 
 Accumulated depreciation values 
 Historical depreciation postings 
 Financial statements / balance sheet reporting 
 Has anyone performed such a conversion in a productive system, and are there any specific risks or SAP notes that should be considered? 
 Any guidance or best practices would be greatly appreciated. 
 Thank you in advance.

title: FOBusinessUnit Replication Error – Locking of Object O XXXXXXXX Was Not Possible
author: AMIT_SHARMA01
text:
Hi Experts, 
 I am facing an issue while replicating a Business Unit (FOBusinessUnit) from SAP SuccessFactors to SAP ECC. 
 During replication, I receive the following error message: 
 Error: 
 FOBusinessUnit XXXXXXXX: Locking of object O XXXXXXXX was not possible 
 I have already checked whether the corresponding organizational object is currently open or being edited in any screens in either SAP SuccessFactors or SAP ECC. However, I could not identify any active session or user locking the object. 
 Despite this, the replication continues to fail with the same locking error. 
 What I have checked so far: 

 Verified that the object is not currently open in any screen in SuccessFactors. 

 Checked the corresponding object in SAP ECC and confirmed that it is not being edited. 

 Retried the replication, but the same error persists. 
 My Questions: 

 What could be the possible reasons for this locking error when no user appears to be editing the object? 

 Is there any way to identify whether the organizational object is locked at the SAP ECC backend level? 

 Are there any specific SAP tables, transactions, or lock entries that should be checked to identify and resolve this issue? 

 Could this be related to an orphaned lock entry or an issue with the replication process? 
 Has anyone encountered a similar issue while replicating Business Units from SuccessFactors to SAP ECC? 
 Any suggestions or guidance on how to identify and resolve the underlying lock would be greatly appreciated. 
 Thanks in advance for your support!

title: AI Is Changing the First Job: Why Youth Employment Belongs on Every Business Agenda
author: Maximilian Herrmann
text:
This summer, researchers at Stanford used U.S. payroll data to see where AI is already changing employment. 
 Explore how SAP turns bold ideas into measurable change for people and planet 

 Learn more 

 Among 22- to 25-year-olds, employment in the jobs most exposed to AI has fallen 19% behind employment in less-exposed jobs. Experienced workers show no such gap.* The change is happening where careers start. 

 Young people were already struggling to find work before AI arrived. According to the International Labor Organization, 257 million young people are not in employment, education, or training—9 million more than in 2023. 

 Over the next decade, around 1.2 billion young people in emerging economies will reach working age, while only about 420 million jobs are expected to be created there, according to the World Bank Group. 

 Why this is a business question 

 Entry-level jobs are where people learn how work actually gets done and build their first professional networks. Over time, they become the experienced staff on which companies rely. If AI takes over many of the tasks that used to make up those first roles, companies may save time today, but they will find it harder to develop their own talent in a few years. 

 SAP has a direct stake in this. Our customers and partners need people who can run the technology they buy, and many of those people will be young professionals starting out in markets where SAP is growing. 

 If young people cannot find a first job, they also miss the experience the digital economy will need from them later. 

 Why the UN General Assembly 

 Many different players shape whether young people find work. Governments shape education systems and labor markets, United Nations (UN) agencies and foundations run programs, and companies decide whom to hire. Each works on its own part, and young people often fall through the gaps in between. 

 UN General Assembly week is one of the few moments each year when these actors are in the same city at the same time. That is why SAP made youth skills and employment a focus there, alongside its long-standing partnership with UNICEF’s Generation Unlimited, whose Board SAP CEO Christian Klein chairs. 

 On a panel at the Generation Unlimited Global Leadership Council, Klein made the case that large AI investments should come with a plan for the people who will work with the technology, including young people looking for their first role. 

 Two ideas ran through the week. The first is that training only pays off when it connects to the next step. The Youth Livelihoods Alliance—which Generation Unlimited launched at SAP’s New York office with SAP, Accenture, and the Standard Chartered Foundation as founding partners—is built on that idea. It links the partners’ programs into one route from first skills to recognized credentials and a job, supported by Yoma, a digital platform where more than 1.3 million young people keep a verified record of what they have learned. 

 “The future of work cannot be built without young people,” said Rashmi Verma, chief inclusion and social impact officer at SAP. “While millions are developing valuable skills, too many still struggle to access meaningful employment. Closing that gap requires stronger collaboration between business, governments, and civil society. By connecting learning opportunities to real jobs, we can help ensure that young people are prepared not only to navigate an AI-powered economy, but to shape it.” 

 The second idea is that companies can contribute most through what they already do. Hiring from the programs they fund, buying from social enterprises, and lending their experts to social innovators can have a lasting effect—and companies can do all of it within their normal operations. 

 SAP works on this with the World Economic Forum, where it co-chairs the Corporate Leadership Council for Social Innovation, and with partners such as EY and Microsoft in Scaling AI for Good, a program that helps social innovators use AI in their work. 

 Next stop: Heidelberg 

 In Heidelberg, near SAP headquarters, young people will lead the discussion. From December 8-10, 2026, the UN Youth Office will host its first UN Youth Townhall. More than 1,000 young people will meet leaders from governments, the UN, academia, and business to develop recommendations on AI, future skills, and work. 

 SAP is a partner of the UN Youth Townhall and plans to support participation by young people from underrepresented backgrounds. 

 For companies, the question is how to turn what they hear in Heidelberg into action: opening routes into work, giving young people opportunities to gain experience, and involving them in decisions about how AI changes their jobs. 

 The conversation may begin at a town hall, but the response belongs in everyday business. 
 Subscribe to our newsletter to receive weekly news, stories, and highlights from the SAP News Center 

 Sign up here 

 *Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen, 2026

title: Month-end close and AI agents: which steps would you actually hand over?
author: Farrukh_Gillani
text:
Hi everyone, 
 I've been reading a lot about Joule agents for finance (accruals, journal entries, clearing) and wanted to bring the discussion back to a normal month-end close. 
 In many S/4HANA companies the close looks like this: 
 order settlement every week, and again at month end 
 allocation percentages updated every quarter, then the allocation runs 
 AuC settlement 
 depreciation run and asset checks 
 GR/IR review and accruals 
 Timing matters. One failed step blocks the next, and the finance team spends a lot of time checking logs and chasing errors. 
 Some of this can already be scheduled with SAP Advanced Financial Closing. SAP is now adding AI agents for accruals and journal entries. But I haven't seen much yet for settlement, allocations or asset closing. 
 So my questions: 
 Which close steps would you trust an AI agent with today, and which only need good scheduling? 
 Where do you think AI adds the most value: running the steps, or the checks before and after (missing settlement rules, error logs, unusual variances)? 
 Is anyone already using AFC together with Joule agents? What worked for you? 
 My view as a finance person: the run itself is usually rule-based and fine with scheduling. The real time goes into the checks and corrections around it, and that's where I'd like AI to help, with the accountant still approving anything that posts. 
 Curious to hear how others see it.
